subject: Throughput measurement protocol and commercial options
messages:
From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@acme.ai>
Date: Tue, 7 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Throughput guarantees and commit question

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated for a production ML inference lane and need to lock down throughput guarantees and the commercial structure. A few concrete items:

- We're targeting ~120k tokens/sec aggregate across our 3 primary endpoints (chat + summarization + rerank). That maps to ~450 req/s during peak windows for our request shape.
- Latency targets: p50 <= 120ms; p95 <= 400ms for the chat endpoint at 32 token context.
- We'd prefer a reserved commit (12‑18 months) with a pricing band tied to committed tokens/sec.

Can you share how Redwood measures tokens/sec and requests/sec for Dedicated, what evidence you provide for a throughput guarantee, and typical commercial discount bands for commits of this size? I'll attach a sanitized trace if that helps.

Appreciate it,
Jared
--
Jared Mills
Head of ML Engineering, Acme.ai
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme.ai>
Cc: Emily Park <emily.park@acme.ai>
Date: Wed, 8 Dec 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantees and commit question

Hi Jared — great to hear these numbers. Short answers first, then a suggested plan:

- Measurement methodology: we report both tokens/sec (aggregate token generation across all GPUs) and requests/sec (completed requests/sec) from the Dedicated control plane. Guarantees are expressed as a tokens/sec floor for a committed pool size plus latency SLOs measured by running a representative workload against the customer's pinned model version for a 60‑minute acceptance window.

- Evidence we provide: (1) an acceptance run report with per‑GPU token/sec and requests/sec breakdowns, (2) latency histograms (p50/p95/p99) for the run, (3) KV/cache hit rates and batching stats.

- Commercial bands: we typically tier discounts by committed tokens/sec and commit length. For a 12–18 month commit across the token volumes you're describing, discounts range from 20–35% off list for the reserved pool (higher discounts for longer commits and volume guarantees). Exact % depends on burst buffer, autoscaling allowances, and termination clauses.

What I'll do next: can you attach a 15–30 minute representative trace (request headers + sizes + arrival timestamps)? We'll run our benchmark script (attached) against a pinned model and return an acceptance report. If you agree, I'll loop in Marissa for the pricing bands and commit paperwork.

Attachment: redwood_benchmark_script.sh (bash script we use for acceptance runs)

Thanks,
Diego
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantees and commit question

Diego — attaching the sanitized workload trace as discussed. Notes:

- File: acme_workload_trace_1209.json (included) — contains timestamps, request sizes, and route ids for a 30‑minute peak period.
- The chat route has a median prompt length of 18 tokens and median generation of 45 tokens. Summarization is bursty but lower token counts.

Questions from our infra team:
1) When you quote tokens/sec guarantee, is that measured on generation tokens only or generation+prompt tokens?
2) How do you handle shared cache scenarios (we will be on a multi‑tenant Redwood Dedicated cluster initially)?

We'd also like clarity on the measurement acceptance window length and whether we can run two separate acceptance runs (one for steady‑state and one for burst).

Thanks — Jared

Attachment: acme_workload_trace_1209.json (application/json)
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Mills <jared.mills@acme.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Emily Park <emily.park@acme.ai>
Date: Sat, 11 Dec 2026 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput guarantees and commit question

Thanks for the trace — that's exactly what we need. Answering your infra Qs inline and proposing commercial options: 

1) tokens/sec definition: our guarantee counts generation tokens only for the committed floor (we exclude prompt tokens from the committed throughput for pricing), but the acceptance report will show both prompt+generation so you can verify end‑to‑end cost.

2) cache and multi‑tenant: Dedicated pools are tenant‑isolated at the service level; you get a customer‑dedicated GPU pool and control plane. If you start on a shared Dedicated cluster during trial, we baseline your cache hit metrics and include a warm‑up / prefix‑cache phase in the acceptance run.

Acceptance window: standard is a single 60‑minute run. We can do two runs (60m steady + 15m burst) as a commercial accommodation; the burst run is used to validate autoscaling and buffer capacity rather than the committed floor.

Commercial options (proposed):
- Option A (12m commit): 20% discount, reserve a 150k tokens/sec floor (generation tokens) with 20% burst buffer for autoscaling.
- Option B (18m commit): 28% discount, 170k tokens/sec floor, 30% burst buffer, priority capacity in region.
- Option C (24m or larger): custom pricing + SLO addendum (we can discuss separately).

I'll run the attached benchmark script against the trace on our CI and return an acceptance report by Monday. Looping in Marissa to draft the commit pricing matrix and legal talking points.

Attachments: throughput_sample_run_1211.log (acceptance run stub), commit_pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (pricing bands)

— Diego
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Throughput measurement protocol and commercial options

Diego / Avery — summary and next steps before we present to Acme: 

Summary:
- Acceptance: run steady‑state 60m + 15m burst; report will include per‑GPU tokens/sec, requests/sec, p50/p95 latency and cache metrics.
- Measurement: committed floor = generation tokens/sec. We'll provide an acceptance report and a one‑page SLO exhibit that codifies measurement method and remediation (credits) for breaches.
- Commercial ask: present Option B as our recommend starting point (18m, 28% discount, 170k floor, 30% burst). Option A is fallback if they want a lower commitment.

Negotiation points to keep flexible: burst buffer %, termination windows, and whether prompt tokens should be included in billing for overages during burst periods. We'll offer a single 90‑day ramp where autoscale burst is charged at on‑demand rate to reduce risk.

Action items: 
- Diego: send acceptance report + SLO exhibit to Jared and Emily by EOD Tuesday (will include the benchmark log we generated).
- Avery: prepare redlines to the standard Dedicated addendum focusing on measurement language and credits.
- Marissa: prepare the draft commercial deck and the DocuSign envelope for Option B.

I'll present the Option B term sheet to Acme in our call on Wednesday.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
